newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - China Eastern starts strongly.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - China Eastern starts strongly.

text.p: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) in China Eastern Airlines Corp Ltd started trading in New York on Tuesday amid strong interest.

The Chinese airline highlighted a largely quiet market in ADRs and foreign shares as many traders waited for news on interest rates from the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday and Wednesday. ADRs also have been jostled recently by volatile trade in the dollar.
"I think everyone's a little bit nervous here, not wanting to get involved," a trader said.

China Eastern, the first Chinese airline to have its shares listed on the New York Stock Exchange, rose 1/2 to 18-1/2. The stock was among the most active on the exchange, with 1.6 million shares traded by late morning.
The company was featured in The New York Times' Market Watch column, which called it "an obvious choice" for investors seeking to latch on to China's expanding economy.
However, columnist Seth Faison said China Eastern was "still opaque about some of its basic operations, like who really runs the airline and how its executives are compensated."
Italy's Fila Holdings SpA fell 4-1/8 to 61-3/4 after Goldman Sachs cut its rating for the clothing, sportswear and footwear company to market outperform from its priority and recommended lists.
ADRs in Swedish biotechnology company Biora AB fell one to 19 as the shares were launched on the Nasdaq. Volume was 754,000 shares by late morning.

Among Latin American ADRs, Argentine telecommunications companies Telefonica de Argentina and Telecom Argentina eased after recent gains prompted by a rate adjustment. Argentina's ombudsman also filed a request that the changes be reversed. Telefonica was down 3/8 to 30-1/2 and Telecom fell 3/4 to 47-1/4. Decliners led advancers by 238 to 235 among 807 ADRs. Volume was 24 million shares. ((--Ian Simpson, Wall Street desk, (212) 859-1879))
